newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco talks now look to insurance carriers - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco talks now look to insurance carriers - WSJ.

text.p: State attorneys general involved in talks with tobacco companies have begun discussing the possibility of turning to insurers in any settlement, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal quoted Louisiana Attorney General Richard Ieyoub as saying they "are now considering the issue of insurance" to determine if the industry should play a role in any settlement that may be reached.

Such a move is sure to meet resistance from property-casualty insurers, which have maintained that policies sold to cigarette makers have included strict product-liability exclusions that preclude claims for any damage awards paid to smokers.

Ieyoub said he and the other attorneys general are "united in trying to consider every possible factor that might enter into settlement negotiations." Tobacco company representatives are expected to issue their response about the insurance question in about a week.
However, Ieyoub added: "If a settlement could be reached that would be satisfactory to all and could be financed without the insurance industry," they may not turn to insurance carriers.

Unnamed sources close to the matter said the talks had recently focused on a settlement package that could total more than $300 billion, payable over 25 years to smokers and states seeking reimbursement for health-care costs associated with smoking-related illnesses.

Maurice Greenberg, chairman of American international Group Inc, which sells property-casualty insurance, said he believed negotiators would have a difficult time involving the insurance industry. "The exclusions are good. And if you don't cover something, you don't pay for it. ... I would hope this is still a constitutional country and the law means something."
